files.contract: File private_data is the shared context, not a private cursor. log uses cont=0; log_cont uses cont=1 and may wait.

Debug extraction preserves underlying ring bytes but advances context-wide nd_read_page and nd_read_offset. An empty extraction can reinitialize shared read_avail. Destructive ipc_log_drop is a distinct writer-space reclamation path.
nd_read_page and per-page nd_read_offset belong to the shared context/pages. Without CONFIG_DEBUG_FS, create_ctx_debugfs is an empty stub.
CONFIG_IPC_LOGGING controls the logging/extract API independently from debugfs.
Creates cnss and cnss-long logging contexts.
32 pages per context; cnss_pr_dbg writes cnss and cnss_pr_vdbg writes cnss-long.
Target capability debug message includes board_id; Downloading BDF debug message includes the actual selected filename. Both use cnss_pr_dbg, not a new caller-generated QMI request.

limits: This is metadata and source evidence, not an empty-log result. No IPC log was opened, so no claim is made about the contents, retention, prior consumption or actual existence of a runtime CNSS context.

The actual owner config disables debugfs while enabling IPC logging; the reviewed public source explains how ring storage can be compiled without a runtime debugfs reader. It is not proof that the owner shipping implementation is byte-identical.
The source's non-destructive terminology refers to ring bytes, not a stateless or per-open cursor. A byte/time cap would not remove that side effect if a reader were available.
The su and PID1 mount views were inspected; this is not an exhaustive scan of every process mount namespace.
No raw mount table, complete kernel configuration, application/process names, network identifiers or log bytes are published.
QMI board ID and the selected stock BDF remain unresolved. The earlier cached BDF customer/project/revision fields and PCI subsystem ID cannot substitute.
No filesystem mount, settings change, radio operation or new kernel capability was introduced to fabricate an endpoint.
